stops.name: Cutty Sark
stops.clue: Start beside the clipper ship that raced tea home from China. Walk round to her bow and look at the figurehead.
stops.question: The figurehead is Nannie the witch from a Robert Burns poem. What is she clutching in her hand?
stops.hint: She snatched it from Tam's grey mare, Meg, as he fled.
stops.fact: Cutty Sark was launched in 1869. Her name comes from Nannie's short shirt in Burns's poem Tam o' Shanter.

stops.name: Foot Tunnel Dome
stops.clue: Head north to the river. Find the round brick building with a glass dome.
stops.question: The dome hides a tunnel under the Thames. Which 'island' does it bring you out on?
stops.fact: The Greenwich Foot Tunnel opened in 1902 so dockworkers could walk to work across the river.

stops.name: The Painted Hall
stops.clue: Walk east along the river into the Old Royal Naval College grounds. Find the Painted Hall, under the western of the two domes.
stops.question: One artist spent 19 years painting the hall's ceiling. What was his surname?
stops.fact: Thornhill worked on the Painted Hall from 1707 to 1726. It is often called Britain's Sistine Chapel.

stops.name: Greenwich Market
stops.clue: Head back towards the town centre and find the covered market. Look up at the words above the entrance arch.
stops.question: The inscription says “A false ______ is abomination to the Lord.” What's the missing word?
stops.hint: It's what a market trader's scales should be.
stops.fact: The line is from Proverbs 11:1, a warning to traders about honest weights.

stops.name: Nelson's Ship in a Bottle
stops.clue: Cross Romney Road to the National Maritime Museum. Find a giant glass bottle with a ship inside.
stops.question: The ship in the bottle is a replica of which admiral's flagship?
stops.hint: His column stands in Trafalgar Square.
stops.fact: Yinka Shonibare's sculpture first sat on Trafalgar Square's Fourth Plinth in 2010, then moved here in 2012.

stops.name: The Queen's House
stops.clue: Walk east to the bright white villa at the edge of the park.
stops.question: Its spiral staircase is named after a flower in the ironwork. Which flower?
stops.fact: Inigo Jones designed the house. The staircase was the first geometric self-supporting spiral stair in Britain.

stops.name: Royal Observatory
stops.clue: Climb the hill through Greenwich Park to the Observatory and the Prime Meridian line.
stops.question: A red ball on the roof drops every day at the same time. What time? (e.g. 3pm)
stops.fact: The time ball has dropped at 13:00 since 1833 so ships on the Thames could set their chronometers.
